newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINE GAME SUSPENDED AFTER CROWD RIOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE GAME SUSPENDED AFTER CROWD RIOT.

text.p: The Argentine league match between Velez Sarsfield and Lanus was suspended 35 minutes into the second half Sunday after the expulsion of Velez goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert set off a crowd riot.
Lanus, playing at home, were winning 3-1 when Chilavert was sent off for furiously complaining to referee Hugo Cordero for awarding an indirect free kick inside the area which led to a Lanus goal.

Enraged Velez fans started to smash up their part of the stadium, and a group rushed onto the pitch to try and catch the referee. They hurled projectiles at police, who responded with rubber bullets and tear gas.
A mob of Lanus supporters then charged the Velez fans.
Police skirmished with rioters outside the stadium before order was reestablished.
Police said they had detained 12 people, all Lanus fans, by the end of the evening.

The burly Chilavert is no stranger to incident. An appeals court Friday confirmed a 13-month ban for punching a stadium assistant during an on-field brawl in 1994, as well as a three-month suspended prison sentence.
Chilavert is appealing the ruling to the Supreme Court.
As captain of his native Paraguay's national team, Chilavert is already serving a four-match FIFA ban on playing in World Cup qualifiers for hitting Colombia striker Faustino Asprilla.
Chilavert, a Paraguayan national hero, says he wants to one day stand for president on a tough law-and-order ticket.
Argentina's soccer body, AFA, will decide whether Lanus is awarded points for its interrupted victory.
If no points were awarded for the game, Lanus would be 18th on the table, and Velez fifth.
